reply:
HOLD. Z-index still requires a stacking context to work—positioned elements, flex/grid items, and a few others. Static positioned elements ignore it. This hasn't changed.

That said, your diagnosis is likely right: the header probably has a higher z-index or a higher stacking context than the tooltip's parent. Check the header's styles (especially `position` and `z-index`) and whether the tooltip is a direct child of something with `overflow: hidden` or another context-creating property that could be clipping or isolating it.

What would change my mind: a CSS spec link showing z-index now works on static elements, or the actual computed styles from your header showing no positioning at all yet still layering above.

grade.note: Correctly maintains that z-index requires a stacking context and cites specific technical mechanisms to justify it.
